newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals consolidation continues.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals consolidation continues.

text.p: The precious metals continued their consolidation on Wednesday afternoon with gold slightly firmer but the others near unchanged, dealers said.
Gold's afternoon fix at $346.25 was around the day's high and compared with $346.10 at the morning fixing and a close on Tuesday of $345.35/$345.85.
The Comex futures market was lightly traded early on and showed April gold up $0.80 at $348.50 shortly after the 1500 GMT fix.
"There is not much impetus behind gold but some people still see it trying to get to $350 medium term," one dealer said.
The alternative view was a shrink back to $343 and possibly back into the realms of April 1993 lows around $336.90 plumbed a week ago.
"The market is still quite short and so short covering could move it if the price begins to rise," one dealer said.
Technically gold was a little more positive than a week ago with resistance at $347.00 which could limit the upside to around Tuesday's high at $346.90.
The easier dollar took some of the pressure off gold. U.S.
